transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-29 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Maya, Tomás, Ravi, Sara, Elliot

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check—are there any urgent blockers before we dive in?
[00:06] Ravi Patel: No urgent, just wanted to get an update on the access side, we saw one error when hitting the gateway yesterday, so curious if that was on our side or Redwood.
[00:14] Sara Nguyen: yeah the 403 came from our egress policy, we patched it but want to be sure the VPC peering thing is set right.
[00:22] Tomás Rivera: Thanks, Sara. We saw the 403 during the handshake - looked like the certificate chain from your proxy didn't include the intermediate. Also your VPC pairing (VPC peering) entry didn't allow the ephemeral ports we use for the control channel. We've got a doc link in the deck — I'll paste after.
[00:37] Elliot Brooks: Also from a security perspective, we need to confirm KMS flows for log encryption and that audit log retention meets our regs.
[00:44] Maya Chen: Absolutely, we will include KMS integration notes. Quick recap: last week we provisioned the private control plane and granted a service account; Sara, you had asked for SAML to be tested with your IDP.
[00:54] Sara Nguyen: Correct. I tried a SAML login but the assertion was rejected. It looked like the audience field was off.
[01:02] Tomás Rivera: Right, that tracks. Our default SP entity ID is slightly different than the value in some IDPs - that's an easy fix. Elliot, can you share the SAML trace? Even a screenshot helps.
[01:11] Elliot Brooks: I'll share. Quick Q on perf: we ran a small load test with 2 concurrent sessions and saw tail latency spikes around 250ms per token on the longest prompts. Is that expected on the dedicated slot?
[01:22] Maya Chen: Not expected if you're pinned to dedicated capacity. A few suspects: continual batching thresholds or KV cache misses. Tomás, can you explain how KV cache behaves on cold starts?
[01:31] Tomás Rivera: Sure—so when a new instance comes up, the KV cache is empty and the first few requests are essentially cold; you see increased latency until the working set warms. For chat workloads with long contexts we also have more cache eviction churn. It sounds like your prompts are long, Ravi?
[01:43] Ravi Patel: We have 4–8k token histories for some agents, yes. But the big spikes aren't only at startup, they happen mid-session occasionally.
[01:51] Tomás Rivera: That could be tokenization differences or prompt prefix expansion. Also we saw in the logs a few "kay vee cash" misses (transcriber note: KV cache). Possible that quantized model variant is doing slightly different memory layout causing cache thrash.
[02:05] Sara Nguyen: Wait, you mentioned quantized model variant — we are currently on the 4-bit profile right? Any tradeoffs we should expect?
[02:12] Maya Chen: Good point. The 4-bit gives significant cost reductions but can change throughput characteristics slightly. For long-context workloads, sometimes 8-bit or mixed precision is steadier. We can recommend a profile based on your latency SLOs.
[02:24] Ravi Patel: Our goal is sub-200ms tail for 99th at 2 concurrent sessions — is that realistic without moving to a bigger instance?
[02:32] Tomás Rivera: It might be tight. We can try conservative batching, keep KV cache warm, and a quantization profile tuned for latency. Also, routing policy can keep requests on a hot instance which helps.
[02:44] Elliot Brooks: On compliance, we need explicit audit logs with user-level attribution for every inference. Does Redwood expose token-level logs or is that abstracted?
[02:53] Maya Chen: We expose per-request metadata, not raw token content by default for privacy, but you can enable deeper logging with KMS-wrapped retention and role-based access. We'll send the security pack that clarifies this.
[03:05] Sara Nguyen: Great. Back to access: I will share CIDR ranges and the one egress rule we blocked — the port range was 31000-32000, is that what you use?
[03:15] Tomás Rivera: Our control plane uses a few ephemeral ranges; 31000-32000 overlaps with one we use for some RPCs, yes. We recommend opening 30000-32767 for the initial test.
[03:25] Ravi Patel: Sounds like a plan. For the dedicated perf run you mentioned, what instrumentation will we get?
[03:32] Tomás Rivera: We'll provide a benchmark sheet with per-request latency, token rates, batch sizes, and the trace IDs. We also include a raw log sample and instruction for reproducing top-tailer cases.
[03:42] Maya Chen: We'll schedule a two-hour window where we run aggressive traffic and you can watch the instance. It helps identify cold starts and mid-session anomalies.
[03:50] Elliot Brooks: On data residency — we need inference to run in eu-west-1 only. Are there any caveats for private deployment?
[03:58] Maya Chen: Private supports region pinning. For hosted, we have region routing; for private we stand up the control plane in your region, there are some latency tradeoffs if your clients are elsewhere. We'll confirm the region playbook.
[04:10] Sara Nguyen: One operational glitch we hit was token accounting — our billing dashboard shows token burn higher than expected, any insight?
[04:17] Tomás Rivera: Could be prompt echo or system prompt duplication. Also caching reduces token counts only when we can reuse prefix states. We'll check your request logs for duplicated prefixes.
[04:27] Ravi Patel: Ok. Next steps from our side: I'll define the set of representative prompts for the perf run and share by Friday.
[04:35] Maya Chen: Excellent. From Redwood: I'll send the security pack and the runbook. Tomás will own the perf scheduling.
[04:41] Tomás Rivera: I'll create the benchmark spreadsheet and invite you to the run. Also I'll paste the doc for VPC pairing, SAML values, and the quick KMS snippet in the chat.
[04:50] Elliot Brooks: One small ask — can you provide a detail on how rollbacks work if we see quality regressions after a quantization change?
[04:58] Maya Chen: Yes, rollbacks are model version pinning plus automatic fallback policy. We'll include an example in the runbook.
[05:06] Sara Nguyen: Great, that helps. Any other business?
[05:09] Ravi Patel: Not from me. Thanks all.
[05:12] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll reconvene the same time next week unless we need an emergency follow-up.

References mentioned: security pack link (placeholder): https://redwood.example.com/security-pack; perf worksheet (placeholder): https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/CRM-78431; VPC pairing doc: https://docs.redwood.example/vpc-peering

End of transcript.
